title: be/get used to ... (I'm used to ...)
subtitle: I'm used to driving on the left
summary: Use be/get used to something or doing something to say that something is not new or strange for you, and keep it apart from I used to do (a past habit).

lesson.heading: Lisa's story
lesson.text: Lisa is American, but she lives in Britain. When she first drove a car in Britain, driving on the left was a problem for her, because Americans drive on the right. She **wasn't used to it**. She **wasn't used to driving** on the left. But after some time, driving on the left became easier. She **got used to driving** on the left. Now it's no problem for Lisa: she **is used to driving** on the left.

examples.text: At first: She **wasn't used to driving** on the left.
After some time: She **got used to driving** on the left.
Now: She **is used to driving** on the left.

lesson.heading: be / get used to
rows: be used to something / doing something
it is not new or strange for me
get used to something / doing something
not be used to something / doing something
it is new or strange for me
She **isn't used to getting up** so early.

lesson.heading: I'm used to something = it is not new or strange for me
lesson.text: Paul lives alone. He has lived alone for a long time, so it is not strange for him. He's used to it. He **is used to living** alone.

examples.text: I bought some new shoes. They felt a little strange at first because I **wasn't used to them**.
Our new apartment is on a busy street. I expect we'll **get used to the noise**, but at the moment it's very disturbing.
Helen has a new job. She has to get up much earlier now than before - at 6.30. She finds this difficult because she **isn't used to getting up** so early.
Katherine's husband is often away from home. She doesn't mind this. She**'s used to him being** away.

lesson.heading: be/get used to doing (not to do)
lesson.text: We say **be/get used to doing something** (not I'm used to do). When we say 'I am used to ...', **to** is a preposition, so the verb ends in -ing. Compare to + infinitive: *We don't want to live here.*

examples.text: Lisa **is used to driving** on the left.
We're not used to **the noise** / **it** / **living here**.

lesson.heading: I am used to doing / I used to do

left.label: I am used to (doing) something
left.text: = it isn't strange or new for me. Present or past: am/was used to.
examples: I**'m used to** the weather here.
I**'m used to driving** on the left because I've lived in Britain a long time.

right.label: I used to do something
right.text: = I did it regularly in the past but no longer do it. Only for the past.
examples: I **used to drive** to work every day, but these days I usually go by bike.
We **used to live** just outside the town, but now we live near the centre.

lesson.text: be/get used to + -ing (I'm used to working nights) is about what feels normal. used to + infinitive (I used to work nights) is a finished past habit.

exercises.prompt: Lisa has lived in Britain for years. She ___ on the left.
exercises.explanation: be used to + -ing: is used to driving (not used to drive).

exercises.prompt: I don't feel good. I stayed up until 3 am. I'm not ___ to bed so late.
exercises.explanation: not be used to + -ing: I'm not used to going to bed so late.

exercises.prompt: My feet hurt. I can't go any further. I'm not ___ so far.
exercises.explanation: It is new and hard for me: I'm not used to walking so far.

exercises.prompt: I like this part of town. I've been here a long time, so I'm ___ here.
exercises.explanation: It is not strange for me any more: I'm used to living here.

exercises.prompt: Is the sentence about something that feels normal to the speaker (be used to doing) or about a past habit (used to do)?
categories: be used to doing - not strange for me
used to do - a past habit

items.text: I'm used to the weather here.
I used to drive to work every day.
We used to live just outside the town.
Lisa is used to driving on the left.
Daniel used to drink a lot of coffee.

exercises.prompt: Sarah is a nurse. A year ago she started working nights. At first it was hard for her. It took her a few months to ___ it.
exercises.explanation: get used to something = it becomes normal for you: took her a few months to get used to it.

exercises.prompt: Jack has to drive two hours to work every morning. When he started this job, he ___ driving two hours to work, but after some time he got used to it.
exercises.explanation: At first it was strange for him: he wasn't used to driving two hours.

exercises.prompt: You sleep on the floor. It's OK for you - you have always slept on the floor. A friend asks: 'Wouldn't you prefer to sleep in a bed?' You: 'No, I'm used to ___.'
exercises.explanation: be used to + -ing: I'm used to sleeping on the floor.

exercises.prompt: Kate moved from a big house to a much smaller one. She found it strange at first. Put the words in order.
exercises.answer: She had to get used to living in a much smaller house.
exercises.explanation: had to get used to + -ing: get used to living.

exercises.prompt: Daniel used to ___ a lot of coffee. Now he prefers tea.
exercises.explanation: used to + infinitive for a past habit that has stopped: used to drink.

exercises.prompt: I'm the boss here! I'm not used to ___ told what to do.
exercises.explanation: be used to + -ing; the passive -ing form is being told.

exercises.statement: There used to be a school here, but it was knocked down a few years ago.
exercises.explanation: Correct. used to + infinitive (used to be) describes a past situation that no longer exists.
